transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Time: 09:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Sherwood Platform), Tom Alvarez (Sherwood Head of ML), Sara Kim (Sherwood Security)

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. i'm ava from redwood inference, ryan — sorry ravi is our systems engineer, he'll jump into the integration parts. can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: yeah hola, i'm priya, platform eng, we own the api gateway and traffic shaping.
[00:18] Tom: tom here, lead ml, i own the models and conv pipeline.
[00:22] Sara: sara, security, responsible for compliance and key mgmt.
[00:26] Ravi: hey all. quick agenda: run through hosted vs dedicated vs private fit, how you might place a gateway or proxy, sdk and langchain adapters, quotas/rate limits, observability hooks and next steps.

[00:45] Ava: start with a quick picture of what sherwood is building?
[00:50] Tom: sure — we're building a tenant-aware chat assistant for our docs and support flows. multi-tenant, needs per-tenant rate limits, and some tenants need data residency e.g. eu-only. throughput target initially about 200 qps burst to 500 for peak, average latency target < 250ms p95 for single-turn queries.
[01:10] Priya: we currently front everything with kong and an internal envoy fleet, and we have a lambda-based fallback path for spikes — but we're rethinking to reduce cold starts.
[01:22] Ava: okay sounds familiar. quick question on models — are you using open models or some proprietary fine-tuned ones?
[01:28] Tom: hybrid. we fine-tune an open base for system prompts and have a couple private Llama variants for on-prem customers. that's why we're curious about private deployment options.
[01:40] Ravi: makes sense. so tradeoffs: hosted gives fastest time-to-value, we manage model infra, and you get streaming and SDKs. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation, while Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control for regulated tenants. each has slightly different integration patterns.
[01:58] Priya: can you expand on the gateway/proxy patterns? we don't want to rewrite our gateway if avoidable.
[02:05] Ravi: yes — three common patterns: 1) direct SDK calls from service to redwood hosted endpoint (simplest), 2) edge gateway/proxy where you put a lightweight sidecar or proxy in front of your services to handle auth, rate-limit, and caching (works with envoy/kong), and 3) a more native sidecar per pod for low-latency, local batching and KV cache reuse. the proxy model fits your kong/envoy approach.
[02:34] Priya: ok, and for sidecars you mean something like a small process that holds the kv cache to avoid reloading the kv across requests?
[02:40] Ravi: exactly — reduce kv-copy and warm-start overhead. helps with long-context performance.
[02:45] Tom: how does that play with langchain/llamaindex — our data stack uses llamaindex for retrieval-augmented generation.
[02:52] Ravi: we have SDK adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex, plus an HTTP gateway endpoint. LangChain adapters are maintained and the SDK has helpers for streaming token callbacks and structured outputs. fair warning: some adapter names can vary in the community; indexing libraries sometimes expect synchronous calls so we provide async helpers.
[03:08] Tom: any gotchas for the llama variants — quantized models etc?
[03:12] Ravi: runtime picks kernels based on quantization and seq lengths; dedicated nodes can use optimized kernels for q4/q8 and reduce cost. there can be slight differences in output compared to CPU-only or different quantization, so we recommend evals/quality checks during rollout.
[03:28] Sara: on security — does redwood integrate with our KMS and SSO? we need enterprise key control and SAML for SSO.
[03:36] Ava: yes — for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and SAML/SSO, RBAC and audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 and the private deployment runbook.
[03:47] Sara: ok do you do token-level redaction or PII masking before logs leave our environment?
[03:52] Ravi: we have configurable telemetry filters and you can disable retention; for Private you can choose zero retention and route logs to your SIEM. hosted can do partial redaction with configurable filters — but for strict compliance Private is recommended.
[04:08] Priya: about rate limits — can we do per-tenant quotas and bursting, and how do you expose that?
[04:14] Ravi: yes per-api-key quotas are standard, and per-route quotas too. we support token-based quotas and request-based. you can set burst windows and we expose headers for remaining quota. also supports backpressure signals (429 + retry-after) and webhook notifications for enforcement events.
[04:33] Priya: do you integrate with our existing kong policies so we don't have to plumb quotas in two places?
[04:38] Ravi: typically you'd enforce a first-layer limit in kong, then rely on Redwood per-tenant quotas as a second guard. we provide an envoy filter and kong plugin reference to make it a straightforward config.
[04:50] Tom: observability — what does the console expose? we need token-level cost, per-route latency, tracing.
[04:57] Ava: console gives per-token cost breakdown, p50/p95 latencies by model and route, and full request traces including prompt length and token counts. we also provide an SDK hook to emit traces to your tracing system (jaeger/zipkin/otlp) and token-level attribution if you opt in.
[05:14] Tom: great — how invasive are the SDK changes to our stack?
[05:18] Ravi: SDK is lightweight. we have node/python/java clients. for LangChain you swap the llm wrapper, for LlamaIndex there is a connector. streaming is supported over websockets or http/2; if you prefer a gateway/proxy model, the integration is just HTTP calls from your services to the proxy which then talks to Redwood.
[05:35] Priya: latency concern — with a proxy in same vpc what's realistic for p95? we need <250ms single-turn.
[05:42] Ravi: with dedicated pools in the same region and local proxy sidecar, 150–250ms p95 is achievable for short contexts (<=1k tokens). longer contexts will push that up; KV cache and prefix caching helps. for hosted, typical p95 in our benchmarks is 180–300ms depending on model and region.
[05:59] Tom: curious about cost controls — can we set per-tenant spend limits and alerts?
[06:05] Ava: yes. you can set hard spend caps per API key and alerts at thresholds. Console also shows forecasts based on recent usage; we can push notifications to slack or webhook.
[06:14] Sara: encryption transit and at rest — hosted is managed; for dedicated we want keys in our KMS. private will be fully within our VPC and you accept our HSM?
[06:22] Ravi: for private we support customer-managed keys and run in your VPC; for HSM integrations we have partners and docs. we'll attach the runbook.
[06:30] Priya: related — how do you handle model updates and rollouts? we need canary and fallback to older version if regression.
[06:36] Ravi: rollouts are first-class: you can pin a percentage to new model, do canary, and automatic fallback policy if regression on eval set. Console exposes rollouts and metrics for A/B.
[06:46] Tom: for our pilot we want to test with LangChain + LlamaIndex retrieval, 2 models (one open quantized, one private), traffic ~200 qps, per-tenant quotas, and EU-residency for specific tenant.
[06:58] Ava: perfect — recommended path is Dedicated with VPC peering for the EU tenant to satisfy residency plus a Private node for the on-prem Llama variants if needed. Pilot SOW usually 6–8 weeks with benchmarking and a ramp.
[07:12] Priya: can we start with hosted to iterate quickly then migrate?
[07:16] Ravi: yes many customers start hosted then move to dedicated. integration patterns remain the same — same API and SDK. you can pin versions and route by tenant.
[07:25] Tom: what's the onboarding time for dedicated? including network peering and firewall config?
[07:29] Ava: roughly 2–4 weeks for initial capacity and peering; private on-prem is longer depending on procurement. we'll add a checklist in the runbook.
[07:38] Priya: test plan — we want simulated traffic with a few large-context sessions, can you run 1M tokens/day sim and measure p95 and cost?
[07:46] Ravi: yes we can schedule a benchmark window. we'll want your traffic profile and sample prompts.
[07:52] Sara: one more on audits — do you provide immutable audit logs for request/response metadata?
[07:57] Ravi: yes, request metadata and user identifiers are logged; payload logging is optional and can be disabled. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM for retention.
[08:08] Ava: ok let's recap next steps — we'll send pricing and SOW, runbook and SOC2 docs, schedule benchmark, you send traffic profile and success metrics.
[08:19] Tom: good — also can you include an example kong plugin config for the proxy?
[08:23] Ravi: yep will attach plugin sample and envoy filter.
[08:27] Priya: thanks all.
[08:30] Sara: thanks.
[08:33] Ava: great talk soon.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-recognition: 'kv cache' heard as 'kay v cache' in some places, 'Redwood' was clear. There were short crosstalk segments at 02:05 and 05:18.

End of meeting.
